footerNote: Reported operating income of $980M includes $79M of income from equity investees; this page shows that in Other income (the same treatment as the Q4 FY26 page), so the operating-profit block reads $902M. Starbucks reports in tenths of millions — lines are rounded to whole millions and tie exactly. Essentially all of the $1,045M of net earnings is attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests were about $0M).

kpis.note: to $9.3B — the China JV conversion replaced store sales with royalties

kpis.note: vs $0.49 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $0.85

kpis.label: Net earnings
kpis.note: +87% YoY, lifted by the $536M divestiture gain

oneTimers: A $536M one-time gain on divesting Starbucks' China retail operations into a joint venture (net proceeds were $2.5B; about 8,000 company-run stores became licensed stores). GAAP EPS of $0.91 sits above non-GAAP EPS of $0.85 mainly because of it.
Restructuring and impairment charges of $303M — store closures and write-downs under 'Back to Starbucks' — versus just $21M a year ago.
otherDetail: A $536M gain on converting Starbucks' China retail business into a joint venture (the stores are now licensed, not company-run), plus $79M of income from equity investees — including that China JV — and $37M of interest and other income, less $135M of interest expense.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales rose 8.1%.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America. Revenue fell 34% because China stores became licensed (paying royalties) instead of company-run, after Starbucks moved them into a joint venture.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales rose 7.9% — more transactions (+4.2%) and bigger tickets (+3.5%). North America comps rose 8.1%: the turnaround is showing up where it matters, in the stores.
takeaways.title: The stores are back

takeaways.text: International revenue fell 34% because about 8,000 China stores stopped being company-run and became licensed under the new joint venture — Starbucks now earns royalties and JV income instead of store sales. That switch is also why total revenue fell 1% despite the strong comps.
takeaways.title: China changed shape, not size

takeaways.text: Reported profit rose 87% to $1.0B, but $536M of it is the one-time gain on the China divestiture. Before that gain, operating profit was $902M — up only modestly, with roughly $0.3B of restructuring charges weighing on it.
takeaways.title: A one-off gain did the profit lifting

verdict: Starbucks' turnaround showed up in the stores — global comparable sales jumped 7.9% — and a $536M gain on the China joint-venture deal lifted reported profit 87% to $1.0B.
